A.text: In primary dentition trauma, lips, mucosa, gingivae and frenula should be examined for lacerations and hematomas.
The lips should also be examined for embedded tooth fragments.

B.text: The guidance specifically calls for soft-tissue examination in primary dentition trauma.

C.text: The mucosa, gingivae and frenula must be examined as well as the lips.

D.text: The lips should be examined for embedded tooth fragments, so assuming the fragment was swallowed is not acceptable.

explanation.text: Primary dentition trauma requires examination of the lips, mucosa, gingivae and frenula for lacerations and hematomas.
A swollen lip with a missing crown fragment calls for examining the lips for embedded tooth fragments.
